title: Relay service skeleton: ws server, health, graceful shutdown
goal: Create the relay service skeleton: a `ws` server on `wss /v1/ws` with the `centcom.v1` subprotocol, health endpoints, config, metrics, a module loader that other relay lanes plug into, and a graceful shutdown that tells clients to reconnect.
scope_in: Node HTTP server + `ws` WebSocketServer at path `/v1/ws`, subprotocol negotiation (`centcom.v1` only), transport `maxPayload` guard of 1 MiB, optional origin allowlist.

`GET /healthz` (always `200 {"status":"ok"}`) and `GET /readyz` (200 only when Redis and DB reachable and migrations at expected version; else 503 `{"status":"degraded","checks":{...}}`; also 503 while draining).
`RelayModule` loader: discovers `apps/relay/src/*/module.ts`, sorts by `order`, calls `register(ctx)`; frame pipeline skeleton (`FramePipeline.use(order, stage)`).
`ConnectionRegistry` (id, remote address hash, state, session id, created_at) and a connection cap (`RELAY_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, default 20000) with overload close 4503.
Close-code table `CloseCode` for all codes in CT-WS-ENVELOPE.
Graceful shutdown on SIGTERM/SIGINT: readyz 503, stop upgrades, send `sys.bye` then close 1001 spread over a 0-5 s jitter window, hard stop after `RELAY_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS` (default 25000).
Build info (`version`, `contract_version` from contracts/index.json) and base metrics.
scope_out: Authentication and hello handling (B038), frame validation (B039), heartbeats (B040), sequencing (B041), rooms (B043), fan-out (B044).
Deployment manifests and Fly config (infra lanes).
build_against: The mock client simulator from B011 (connect, send raw text frames, observe closes) and in-memory B009 Redis/KV; DB readiness is checked against the B010 Postgres container or a stub `ReadinessProbe`.
interfaces: WS: `wss://<host>/v1/ws`, subprotocol `centcom.v1`; no token in URL (a request carrying `?ticket=` or `?token=` is refused 400).

TS: `interface RelayModule { name: string; order: number; register(ctx: RelayContext): void | Promise<void> }` and `interface RelayContext { config: RelayConfig; log: Logger; metrics: Metrics; clock: Clock; redis: RedisLike; db: Db; connections: ConnectionRegistry; pipeline: FramePipeline; onShutdown(fn: () => Promise<void>): void; onConnection(h: (c: RelayConnection) => void): void }`
TS: `type InboundStage = (fc: FrameContext, next: () => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>`; reserved stage orders: decode 10, handshake 15, authorise 20, privacy 30, sequence 40, fan-out 50.

TS: `const CloseCode = { Normal: 1000, GoingAway: 1001, ProtocolViolation: 4400, Unauthenticated: 4401, Forbidden: 4403, NotFound: 4404, HandshakeTimeout: 4408, Superseded: 4409, ClientTooOld: 4426, RateLimited: 4429, Overloaded: 4503 } as const`.
acceptance: `GET /healthz` returns 200 `{"status":"ok"}` in < 10 ms even when Redis and Postgres are down; `GET /readyz` returns 503 with `checks.redis.ok=false` within 2 s when Redis is unreachable and 200 when everything is up.
A WebSocket upgrade offering only subprotocol `foo` is refused (HTTP 400); offering `centcom.v1` succeeds and the response echoes `centcom.v1`; upgrade on any other path returns 404.
With `RELAY_MAX_CONNECTIONS=2`, the third connection is accepted, receives a `sys.error` (status 503, `retry_after_s` present) and is closed 4503 within 1 s.

On SIGTERM `readyz` flips to 503 within 100 ms, new upgrades get 503, each existing connection receives `sys.bye` with `p.reason = "server_restart"` and closes with 1001 spread across 0-5 s (all 200 test connections closed within 5.5 s), and the process exits 0 within `RELAY_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_MS`.
A connection still open at the drain deadline is terminated and the process exits with code 0 after logging `shutdown.forced` with the count.
Two stub modules with orders 30 and 10 are registered in order 10 then 30; a module throwing in `register` aborts startup with a non-zero exit and a log line naming the module.

Metrics `relay_connections_active`, `relay_connections_total`, `relay_frames_in_total{t}`, `relay_closes_total{code}` exist and update during a 100-connection test; no metric label contains a session, member or user id.
Startup log line contains `version` and `contract_version` equal to contracts/index.json `contract_version`.
tests: relay.health.test.ts: liveness independent of dependencies, readiness matrix (redis down, db down, migration behind, draining).
relay.upgrade.test.ts: subprotocol, path, query-token refusal, origin allowlist.
relay.shutdown.test.ts: jittered 1001 close, forced stop, exit code (fake timers).
relay.modules.test.ts: ordering and failure of module registration.
guardrails: `/healthz` MUST NOT touch any dependency (CT-STATUS); `/readyz` MUST fail while draining so the load balancer stops routing.
Tickets and tokens MUST NOT be accepted in the URL or query string and MUST NOT be logged; the logger redacts the `Authorization`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` and query string.
The transport `maxPayload` guard MUST be set (1 MiB default) so a hostile client cannot force unbounded buffering; the 256 KiB frame rule itself is enforced in B039.
Shutdown close codes MUST be 1001 with jitter; a synchronized mass close is a thundering-herd bug.
Per-connection state MUST be bounded; the registry MUST remove an entry on every close path (error, timeout, shutdown).
No global mutable singletons: clock, logger, Redis, DB are injected through `RelayContext`.
failure_modes: Redis down at boot -> process starts but `readyz` is 503; connections are refused with 4503 until healthy.
Unhandled exception in a connection handler -> that connection is closed 4400/1011-class with a generic `sys.error`, the process stays up, `relay_handler_errors_total` increments.
SIGTERM during startup -> exit 0 without accepting traffic.
Port already in use -> exit non-zero with a clear log line.
notes: Module auto-discovery (`apps/relay/src/*/module.ts`) is the integration mechanism that keeps relay lanes' deliverables disjoint; downstream lanes B038-B050 export a default `RelayModule` from their own folder.
